strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 8+ benchmarks including real robot validation with credible 72% success rate on 8 tasks
Well-motivated problem addressing real limitations in VLA models (data scarcity and heterogeneity) with clear positioning
Practical approach using object-centric rather than agent-centric representations enables better cross-embodiment generalization
Strong spatial reasoning benchmark results (rank 1.3, 80.9 avg) competitive with GPT-4o despite being open-source 13B model
Substantial improvement on visual aids generation tasks (61.82% on VABench-Point vs 19.09% for RoboPoint, 3.2x improvement)
New VABench benchmark with 300 manually annotated examples addresses evaluation gap for visual aids generation
Ablation studies demonstrate importance of proposed components (SrCoT, self-consistency alignment)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and intuitive motivation from human reasoning processes
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (CoT, spatial relationship graphs, visual traces); SrCoT is reasonable but incremental contribution

Data quality and construction concerns: heavy reliance on automated generation with multiple tool dependencies (GPT-4o, GroundedSAM, Metric3Dv2, Cotracker) but no quantitative quality metrics or error analysis reported

Significant 2D limitation inadequately addressed: restricting to 2D trajectories due to 'limited 3D data' but doesn't explain why 3D cannot be extracted from embodied datasets; 2D-to-3D conversion via back-projection is lossy
Insufficient statistical rigor: SimplerEnv results from 24 episodes with no confidence intervals; real robot 72% figure lacks error bars and trial counts; no significance testing
Real robot evaluation limited in scope: only 8 tasks on xArm with unclear statistical validity; no failure case analysis; comparison baselines limited to RoboPoint and GPT-4o

Zero-shot evaluation unclear: model trained on BridgeData, RT-X, DROID; no clear protocol for held-out evaluation or definition of what constitutes 'unseen' scenarios; potential data overlap with test tasks

Reproducibility concerns: no released code; complex automated data pipeline difficult to reproduce; critical implementation details in appendices; exact prompts and filtering criteria not fully specified
Insufficient analysis of mechanisms: ablations show what helps but not why; self-consistency mechanism vague; no investigation of learned spatial relationships or performance scaling with data
VABench benchmark limitations: only 300 problems; GPT Score (0-10 MLLM evaluation) not fully objective; multiple valid solutions not systematically handled; no inter-annotator agreement metrics
Baseline concerns: OpenVLA at 1.0% seems suspiciously low; DINOv2 Predictor appears to be newly created baseline; recent spatial VLMs not compared directly on manipulation tasks

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across 5 spatial benchmarks, embodied reference tasks, a new benchmark (VABench), simulation, and real-world robotic experiments with strong results
Well-motivated approach addressing real challenges in robotic manipulation (data scarcity and embodiment heterogeneity) through intuitive intermediate spatial representations
Substantial dataset contribution: 300K automatically-constructed SFT data across 10+ embodiments with systematic 5-level capability hierarchy
Solid real-world demonstration: 72% success rate on 8 robotic tasks, with 30% improvement over baseline methods in zero-shot deployment
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (particularly Figures 3 and 6 showing spatial relationship graphs and step-by-step reasoning)
Meaningful ablation studies (Table 3) demonstrating contributions of both SrCoT and self-consistency alignment mechanisms
Introduction of VABench, addressing a gap in benchmarking visual aids generation capabilities
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: chain-of-thought reasoning is established, visual aids for manipulation explored (LLaRVA, EmbodiedCoT), and self-consistency is straightforward—mainly combining existing ideas with spatial relationship graphs

Significant reproducibility concerns: heavy reliance on closed-source models (GPT-4o) for automatic data generation, no code/model release mentioned, and limited transparency on data quality validation procedures and error rates in automatic pipelines

Acknowledged limitation to 2D trajectories with insufficient analysis of impact: fixed 8-point discretization seems restrictive for complex 3D manipulation, and no systematic evaluation of performance degradation for 3D-heavy tasks

Baseline comparison issues: real-world baselines (RoboPoint, GPT-4o) are relatively weak and limited to endpoint prediction; SimplerEnv training data composition not clearly specified for fair comparison; concurrent work (RoboBrain) relegated to appendix

Insufficient statistical rigor: only 24 episodes per SimplerEnv task, no confidence intervals or error bars reported, 8 real-world tasks is limited, and unclear if baseline methods tested on identical task distributions
Limited analysis of design choices: no justification for 8-point traces, 5-level hierarchy, or criteria for selecting visual aid types at inference; missing sensitivity analyses
Narrow real-world validation scope: single robot platform (xArm 6) tested, limiting validation of embodiment heterogeneity claims; only 8 tabletop tasks without diverse manipulation types
Insufficient failure analysis: no systematic error analysis, discussion of failure modes, or qualitative failure case studies to understand method limitations

Missing technical details and computational analysis: sparse details on inverse task construction for self-consistency, accuracy of automatic spatial relationship extraction, and no training/inference time or computational cost reported
